neighbours.label: the token that sets up a price verb: the word right before 'cost' in 'how much does it', 'used to', 'would reportedly'
fire: Before you sign, ask how much does it cost to cancel the plan?
I wonder how much did that cost the city in overtime.
So how much will it cost to replace the roof this year?
The new stadium was originally estimated to cost about 900 million.
Tell me, how much does it cost to rent a boat for a day?
Honestly, how much would it cost to ship the piano to Spain?
A single ticket on that route can easily cost over two hundred dollars.
My friend asked how much does a new bike cost these days.
quiet: Before you sign, ask how long does it take to cancel the plan?
I wonder how often did that happen to the city in winter.
So how soon will it start to rain on the roof this year?
The new stadium was originally designed to hold about ninety thousand.
Tell me, how far is it to the harbour where the boats are?
Honestly, why would it matter if we shipped the piano to Spain?
A single ticket on that route lets you travel all day.
My friend asked where does a new bike go in the garage.

predictions: Fires on the token before 'cost' when the lead-in is a price question or estimate; quiet on the same position in how-long / how-often questions and non-price frames.
notes: Probe: 'How much does it' 0.91 whether the next word is cost or weigh (the unit cannot see ahead); 'How long does it' 0.25; 'would reportedly' 0.34, 'used to' 0.26 regardless of the following verb. So the setup carries it, and the near misses change the lead-in.
